paragraphs.en: Hide your fleet and find your opponent's. Battleship is a two-player game: place your ships in secret, then take turns firing at squares on the other player's board. Sink their whole fleet before they sink yours.
Each player has a 10-by-10 board, with columns A to J and rows 1 to 10. A ship occupies a straight line of squares, horizontally or vertically.
The standard fleet has ten ships:
- One four-square ship.
- Two three-square ships.
- Three two-square ships.
- Four single-square ships.
Ships must fit on the board without overlapping. Leave a gap between them: they may not touch, even at a corner.
At the start, use the arrows to choose random or manual placement and confirm with Enter. Random placement sets up your whole fleet; play can begin once the opponent is ready too.

For manual placement, move around the board with the arrows. Press Enter at one end of a ship, move to its other end and press Enter again. Select the same square twice for a single-square ship. Place ships in any order, provided you still have one of the chosen length.
Backspace cancels a selected first endpoint. If no endpoint is selected, it takes back the last ship you placed.
Once the whole fleet is in place, confirm it by choosing Yes and pressing Enter. Choose No to change the last ship. You cannot move ships after confirming the fleet.
When both fleets are ready, the first player opens fire. On the opponent's board, select a square with the arrows and press Enter. You cannot fire at the same square twice.
You will hear one of these results:
- A miss means there is no ship on that square.
- A hit reveals one square of an enemy ship.
- Sunk means you have hit every square of that ship.
Every shot ends your turn, including a hit or a sinking.
Press Tab to inspect your own board, including the opponent's hits and your surviving ships. Shift+Tab returns to the board where you fire.
The shot that sinks the opponent's final ship wins the game. During play, F reads how many of your fleet's squares remain unhit; Shift+F gives the same count for the enemy fleet.
Before play, you can choose a five-ship fleet instead of the standard ten:
- One five-square ship.
- One four-square ship.
- Two three-square ships.
- One two-square ship.
A separate option allows ships to touch along their sides or corners. They must still fit on the board and cannot overlap.
Arrows: explore the board.
Enter: confirm a placement method, select a ship endpoint during setup, or fire at an enemy square during play.
Backspace: cancel the first endpoint; if none is selected, undo the last ship before confirming the fleet.
F: read your fleet's unhit square count.
Shift+F: read the enemy fleet's unhit square count.
L: read the latest shot whose result is known.
M: read your shots, hits and ships sunk.
Ctrl+L: review your shots and their results.
T: read whose turn it is.
